correctness.rationale: For F_h(z)=z+hKA sin z modulo 2π, u=A sin z, w=Ku, q=u^TKu, Taylor integral identity separates V(z)−V(F_hz) into h(1−hΛ/2)q + (h²/2)(Λq−w^TAw) + h²Σ_i a_i w_i²∫(1−t)(1+cos(z_i+thw_i))dt, all nonnegative when h≤2/Λ and strictly positive whenever sin z≠0 (K invertible and nonconstant cosine segment). Compactness and vanishing increments force every orbit to converge to one of finitely many binary equilibria, even at equality. All other binary equilibria have expanding derivative direction by symmetric congruence. Analytic nonzero Jacobian determinant at zero makes all preimages of null sets null; an endomorphism center-stable theorem gives null basin of each unstable fixed point despite singular derivatives. For h>2/Λ p* derivative has eigenvalue <−1, so same N^-1 argument makes its basin null. Direct independent numerical integration at critical parameter for nontrivial points verified Taylor equality to high precision; analysis does not infer measure theory from numerics.
residual_risks: Finite checks corroborate analytical arguments, not arbitrary real-parameter universality.

value.rationale: The inclusive threshold 2/Λ for almost-everywhere attraction of a prescribed phase-opposition state is a natural stability boundary for positive-weight tree phase networks. Exact endpoint descent persists when the usual quadratic descent coefficient vanishes; noninvertibility occurs at smaller steps than loss of almost-global attraction. Closing this measure-theoretic gap is meaningful beyond a local multiplier check and does not purport to classify supercritical attractors.
